boundaries: 6 Oct 2026 ultrasound × hypnosis intersection sweep: six research lanes searched English, Latin American / Iberian, South Asian, East / Southeast Asian, European / MENA, adult / erotic and vertical-microdrama sources. The intersection is genuinely near-empty: 1 source-supported record was added and 3 existing records were enriched.

Inclusion caveats: Yehh Jadu Hai Jinn Ka! hypnotizes Rehan rather than pregnant Roshni; Art of the Devil reverses the control direction because Boom commissions the ritual magic; Rosemary’s Baby (2014) uses cult gaslighting and manipulation rather than literal hypnosis. Daayan is the strongest direct scan-to-hypnosis match.

Not promoted: Unter uns and Demain nous appartient have hypnosis and pregnancy but no sourced ultrasound scene; 25 verified near-misses and 4 unverified leads remain outside the catalog. The Handmaid’s Tale season 2 is borderline institutional indoctrination rather than hypnosis, and Ultrasound (2021) has no verifiable sonogram scene despite its title.

Intersection coverage gaps remain for poorly indexed anthology episodes, Burmese-language sources, episode-level Turkish / Arabic serials and app-only microdramas. Dedicated adult / erotic passes found no verifiable title combining a pregnancy scan with hypnosis, love-potion or qualifying control; possession-only stories were excluded.

5 Oct 2026 pregnancy-ultrasound sweep: 84 confirmed scene-level records across 9 categories. The 107 near-misses remain excluded, and 13 titles already present elsewhere in the catalog were not added again.

Ultrasound coverage: 12 languages and four formats (59 TV-series records, 22 movies, 2 soap operas and 1 TV movie). Latin American research produced 19 records, with fake-pregnancy fraud the dominant pattern; Indian research found no prenatal-sex-determination reveal, consistent with the PCPNDT Act prohibition.

Ultrasound gaps for a future pass: Japanese and Chinese drama, Scandinavian and German television, Arabic and Persian fiction, and pornographic-industry titles. The Good Doctor episode numbering remains uncertain, and The Pregnancy Project is the weakest confirmed inclusion.

Nine existing catalog records were cross-checked as ultrasound overlaps: Superstore, Coronation Street, Emmerdale, Days of Our Lives, General Hospital, The Young and the Restless, Un medico in famiglia, Sasural Simar Ka and Knocked Up. They remain single records rather than duplicates; the supplied merge packet did not include scene-level overlap synopses or direct overlap source links.

5 Oct 2026 surrogate sweep: a worldwide nine-lane search found 1 confirmed and 2 probable records, with 24+ near-misses ruled out. The trope is nearly nonexistent worldwide; India, Latin America / Spanish-Portuguese, Turkey / MENA, adult / erotic worldwide and vertical-short lanes returned no qualifying title.

Surrogate-sweep caveats: Days of Our Lives combines chemical control concurrent with Marlena’s surrogacy and separate later hypnosis / brainwashing arcs; The Young and the Restless places Mariah’s reported brainwashing about four years after her surrogacy and leaves the controller’s presence ambiguous; Toni, männlich, Hebamme is a borderline coercive domestic-control case, not literal hypnosis.

5 Oct 2026 re-sweep: eight source-supported records were added and Sleep, My Love (1948) was folded into the rich-woman money / inheritance category without duplication. Two October theatrical titles were still upcoming at research time, and Hypnotized Bride remains explicitly probable because only one licensed short-drama channel supports its plot.

Wife-takes-husband-to-hypnotist follow-up: no new qualifying title was found. Holiday Hypnosis (2005) and Edison’s Mesmerist and Country Couple (1899) were confirmed only as non-qualifying near-misses; the Chinese vertical short The Hypnotized Her was held out because the required plot turn could not be verified.

Vertical-short coverage gap: searches covered ReelShort, DramaBox, FlexTV, ShortMax, NetShort, DramaWave, Chinese mini-programs and social-video serials, but app catalogs remain poorly discoverable. Only one eligible single-source vertical-short candidate was added, so this is a coverage limitation rather than an absence claim; a dedicated app-catalog pass remains open.

Partner-to-hypnotist switched-target pattern: the worldwide search found no exact match. “The Hypnotist” (1936), in which both spouses are hypnotized, and “How to Be Very, Very Popular” (1955), in which a woman is hypnotized instead of an intended male target, are both loose matches because neither available synopsis establishes that she brought a male partner for his treatment. The other 13 reviewed titles are retained only as clearly labeled non-qualifying near-misses.

Two additional leads remain unverified because plot sources were insufficient: the Mexican film “El hipnotizador / The Hypnotist” (1940) and the German comedy “Hypnotisiert” (IMDb tt0658815). Targeted searches found no qualifying titles in Indian regional cinema, European film beyond the listed cases, Latin American telenovelas, Korean/Japanese/Chinese dramas or Turkish dizis.
